title: Combination circuits
target: Reduce a circuit by identifying genuine series and parallel groups.
criteria: Reduce one group at a time.
Check current and voltage conservation in the original circuit.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A circuit has A from node P to Q. Resistors B and C both connect Q to R. Which first grouping is valid?
options: B and C form a parallel group.
B and C are necessarily series.
A and B are parallel because both touch Q.
cpa.guide: Parallel components must share both nodes, not just one.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: An 8 Ω resistor and another 8 Ω resistor share both endpoint nodes; their group is in series with 5 Ω. Which reduction order is valid?
options: Reduce the parallel pair, then add the 5 Ω series resistance.
Subtract 5 Ω from either branch before reducing.
cpa.guide: Identify topology first; the equal parallel pair reduces to 4 Ω.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Two 10 Ω resistors in parallel form a group in series with 7 Ω. What is total resistance?
cpa.guide: The pair is 5 Ω; add 7 Ω to get 12 Ω.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 24 V supply drives a 4 Ω series resistor and a parallel group equivalent to 8 Ω. What is total current?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 2 A current reaches two equal parallel branches. What current passes through each branch?
cpa.guide: Equal branch resistances at equal voltage split the total current equally.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A circuit has total current 1.5 A through a 6 Ω series resistor before a parallel group. Supply voltage is 21 V. What is voltage across each branch in the group?
cpa.guide: The series resistor drops 1.5 × 6 = 9 V; the group has 21 − 9 = 12 V across every branch.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
